# D181 Results of the four future recurrence test

2026-10-10. **Population complete and saved checks passed; formal audit launched, completion not yet reviewed.** [All fixed tables](POPULATION_TABLES.md), [scientific protocol](PROTOCOL_V1.md), [execution contract](POPULATION_EXECUTION_V1.md).

## Plain language result

The small aligned-writing lead survives fresh randomness in this model. Some record differences depend on the recipient's reconstruction setting, and that pattern recurs in both preselected pairs of new futures. Three record-pair rankings reverse between the lowest and highest settings in the same direction in all four fresh futures. The effect remains secondary and small relative to the differences between records themselves.

The focal ordinary-writing comparison is mixed, not empty. Its average matching estimate is now positive, but the two fixed future pairs disagree in sign and no ranking reversal agrees across all four futures. Better records generally remain better, and weaker coupling improves average B retention in every donor.

Aligned writing retains more B information than ordinary writing, but does not preserve the complete starting shape or match protected copying. These results strengthen a limited lead about reconstruction depending on both record and recipient. They do not establish better prediction, autonomous repair, or generality beyond these four reused founder blocks.

## Completed panel and verification

The run finished at **16:53:55 UTC on 10 October**, in **1,860.612362636 seconds (31m01s)**, using four spawned single-threaded workers within CPUs 0--5. The frozen conservative allowance was 78m31s. No cases were dropped, retried or excluded.

All four donor blocks 90000/90005/90010/90015, four lives per block and both target families remain: **32 F0 records**. Each has four fresh futures (2,3,4,5), three coupling settings (0.75,1.0,1.25), ordinary/aligned writing and four controls. Three complete replacements precede common/native terminal assays: **2,304 lineages, 6,912 serial read/write pairs and 4,608 assay rows**. These are not independent founders.

Full independent dynamics replay matched reader, writer and terminal states exactly. All 11,648 alias checks passed. Maximum selector/feature/measurement discrepancies were 1.3323e-15, 9.9920e-16 and 2.2204e-16. All 34 output files remain.

The user-requested status verified 213 inherited input hashes, 312 science/qualification hashes, all output hashes, manifest, log and 11 launch-document hashes. A 102.44s read-only check revalidated every saved life, measurement and fixed statistic, forbidding new dynamics and production summary construction. Its proof matched COMPLETE. The separate formal audit is still awaiting user-advanced receipt review.

## Focal common reader B ordinary result

Preference points are 100 times terminal own-minus-alternative preference, not success percentages. Positive favors the intended family; negative favors the alternative. The common final reader is fixed, so these assess retained-record utility for that reader.

| Reconstruction coupling | B ordinary points | B aligned points |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0.75 | 19.0002 | 26.1475 |
| 1.00 | 14.9170 | 24.5667 |
| 1.25 | 12.6770 | 22.3633 |
| Pooled | 15.5314 | 24.3591 |

Ordinary B low-minus-high coupling is **+6.3232 points**, versus +5.8838 in D180. Every donor and donor omission retains this direction. That does not imply every individual record does so, or strict monotonicity in every donor.

Fresh-only signed components in original squared-score units are record **+0.0205439384**, recipient **+0.000663622662**, interaction **+0.000430489028**, total **+0.0216380501**. Record differences remain largest. The positive interaction average conceals pair sensitivity:

| Common B interaction | D180 old 0,1 | Fresh 2,3 | Fresh 4,5 | Six fresh pair mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary focal | -0.000292466746 | -0.000073750814 | +0.000675479571 | +0.000430489028 |
| Aligned secondary | +0.000404609574 | +0.000724911690 | +0.000392940309 | +0.000452421330 |

Three of six ordinary pair products and two individual donor interaction descriptions are negative. All donor/future omission averages are positive: donor-omission range +0.0000880677 to +0.0005669633, future-omission range +0.0001023125 to +0.0010084090. These are sensitivity summaries, not confidence bounds. The result establishes neither no matching nor uniformly recurring ordinary matching.

Ordinary four-future ranking correlations are 0.964706, 0.926471 and 0.979412. Mean ranks reverse 7, 9 and 4 of 120 overlapping record pairs, but **zero reversals agree across all four futures**. Fixed two-future consistency counts remain 2/3/0 and 0/1/0.

## Secondary aligned B recurrence

Aligned B interaction is positive in **both fixed disjoint pairs and all six fresh products**. Its mean **+0.000452421330** is close in scale to D180's +0.000404609574. All four donor descriptions and all donor/future omissions remain positive. Donor-omission range: +0.0003545078 to +0.0005625992; future-omission range: +0.0003609172 to +0.0005126706. A single misleading original noise pair is therefore a less satisfactory explanation of the observed aligned pattern.

Aligned record/recipient/total components are +0.0226629321, +0.000237049880 and +0.0233524033. Ordinary and aligned interaction averages have similar magnitudes. **Greater consistency does not establish a larger aligned interaction**, or a statistically resolved comparison between mechanisms.

Four-future aligned reversal-consistency counts are 0/3/0 across the three recipient-setting pairs. Three reversals between the extremes agree across all four futures. Fixed-pair counts are 1/3/0 and 3/7/0. Record-pair counts overlap and are not independent trials. The four-future criterion is stricter than D180's two-future rule; comparing raw counts does not measure an improvement rate.

Lower coupling has a pooled aligned advantage of **3.7842 points**, but donor 90010 has the opposite mean direction (-0.2930 points). No setting is established as best for every record. Coupling changes both serial reading and writing, so the experiment does not localize their effects.

## Other groups and generalization limits

Native-reader B repeats the contrast: ordinary fixed pairs disagree in sign; aligned has positive estimates in both pairs, all six products and all donor/future omissions. Native aligned mean interaction is +0.000462780396. Native outcomes remain secondary.

Family A has much higher common-reader preferences: **43.5974 ordinary, 43.8761 aligned, 42.8955 protected-copy points**. Its common-reader interactions are much smaller (+0.00000406415 and +0.00000324845); native ordinary is negative and native aligned has mixed fixed pairs. B findings do not generalize automatically across families. All eight groups and negative components remain in the tables.

Fresh futures are new noise realizations, not fresh acquired records or independent populations. Pair products share futures and omission summaries share data. No population interval, p-value, equivalence threshold, variance percentage or prediction ceiling is reported. Aligned B was chosen after D180 and remains secondary.

## Controls and continuing shape loss

Common-reader B scores **28.7903 points protected copying**, **15.5314 ordinary**, **24.3591 aligned**. Alignment adds **8.8277 points** over ordinary but stays **4.4312 below copying**. Ordinary/aligned read-off scores are -16.5751/-17.8609, write-off -3.0273. All five contrasts and every control cell remain. Disabled conditions can express the apparatus's A preference and need not score zero.

Controls support causal carrier use and renewal, not preservation of all content:

| B condition | Starting own shape correlation | Final own shape correlation | Guide retains B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary | 0.794609 | 0.515494 | 153/192 |
| Aligned | 0.794609 | 0.655117 | 184/192 |
| Protected copy | 0.794609 | 0.794609 | 192/192 |

Recognition remains high despite continuous degradation. Counts are labelled paths, not independent founders. Common/native shape and guide measurements are aliases. Every terminal guide label/address is retained, including wrong and unassigned labels.

Terminal clipping reaches **2 of 256 sites (0.78125%)** in native A protected copying; other groups reach at most one site. These are terminal diagnostics, not an assertion about all intermediate states. RMS and clipped-site summaries remain.

## Meaning for L20 and prediction

L20 concerns acquired content being written and reconstructed. These controls distinguish carrier use and renewal from intact copying; shape scores distinguish recognition from fidelity. The repeated aligned signal adds a bounded finding: retained usefulness can depend on the record and reconstruction setting even under a common final reader.

This is an explicit simulated extension with supplied guide and coupling variation, not discovered biological diversity, functional concepts or autonomous interface repair. The carrier is 2,048 bytes, not the earlier 64-byte DoorKey germ. It does not validate every original L20 claim.

For prediction this identifies candidate structure, but does **not** show a challenge reveals it better than equally costly passive observation or starting-only measurements. No predictor or prospective forecast was tested. D141/D162 remain unresolved; D174/D176 negative findings stand. **L20 remains STRESS_TESTED / MIXED.**

After audit closeout, decide whether to test recurrence on fresh founders or return to a preregistered recipient-aware prediction comparison with the starting-only baseline prominent. Neither is registered or launched here.

## Computation storage and audit boundary

Population runtime was 31m01s. The complete disposable benchmark took 18m52s; together **49m52.52s** wall time excluding qualification and audits. Wall time is not a measured CPU-time total. No reporting dynamics or fitting were required.

Population outputs total **522,648,073 bytes (498.44 MiB)**. Pre-audit-launch new-stage inventory was **706,933,382 bytes (674.18 MiB)**, including retained benchmark/qualification; subsequent small receipts are additional. Numerical data, logs, fixtures and caches are external on /mnt/bioIce1. The fixed 1 GiB stage cap, 4 GiB free reserve and separate D180 retention remain.

Formal audit startup was acknowledged **18:08:37 UTC**, PID **1286777**, on 10 October. The frozen audit forbids dynamics and production summary construction. One numerical thread/process stays within CPUs 0--5. Its conservative frozen gate is 78m31s, so it is detached, though the previous read-only saved check took 102.44s. Completion is not assumed. There has been no post-ack audit log/output/process inspection, retry or successor.
